name: Constant yearly growth of data-centre capacity additions
basis_note: Specified by the project owner as about 15% a year. The first year's addition is solved so that total additions equal the IEA capacity for the target year minus 2024

name: EV sales (BEV, PHEV, share) in 2030 between the 2025 actuals and the IEA 2035 scenario
basis_note: The IEA file has no 2030 projection. Two paths are shown: a straight line and constant yearly growth, each applied to BEV, PHEV, EV total and EV share. 2035 is shown direct from the IEA

name: Copper in every non-EV new car
basis_note: The non-EV group is treated as a mid-size internal-combustion car (S11, 18-22 kg). Hybrids are inside this group and have about 39-45 kg (S11); the IEA data cannot split them out, so a bounding case is shown

name: Data-centre capacity added evenly each year to the target year
basis_note: Average yearly addition between 2024 and the target year; the actual yearly build is unknown

name: Base-year data-centre build that is subtracted
basis_note: Mid and high: the 2023 to 2024 addition from the IEA annex (97 - 83 = 14 GW, rounded inputs). Low: the 2020 to 2024 average (37 / 4 = 9.25 GW). Each is a single rounded number from S15

name: Capacity basis for copper per MW
basis_note: Main result on total installed capacity, a prominent second result on IT capacity. The sources behind the 30-40 t/MW do not say which basis they use (known_issues K01)
